categories.main_business_segments: As of 2023, Verisk operates as a single reportable segment focused on Insurance, having divested its Energy, Specialized Markets, and Financial Services businesses. The Insurance segment primarily serves property and casualty (P&C) insurance customers, offering solutions across underwriting, claims, catastrophe modeling, life insurance, specialty business, and marketing solutions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Verisk leverages proprietary and contributory data assets, advanced analytics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and cloud-based platforms to deliver its solutions. The company maintains one of the world's largest private insurance databases, employs predictive modeling, and integrates geospatial, remote sensing, and digital workflow tools to support client decision-making and operational efficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Verisk's primary customers are the top 100 U.S. P&C insurance providers, global reinsurers, InsurTech companies, and insurers in international markets. The company also serves government agencies, self-insurers, third-party administrators, and insurance repair contractors, with additional offerings for life and annuity insurers and specialty insurance markets such as the London market.
categories.geographic_coverage: Verisk operates globally, with a strong presence in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Ireland, Continental Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, China, and other regions. The company’s solutions are used in over 120 countries, with significant operations and customer bases in North America and Europe.
categories.supply_chain_position: Verisk operates as a data, analytics, and technology provider, positioning itself as an upstream and midstream enabler within the insurance value chain. It supplies critical data, analytics, and workflow solutions that support insurers, reinsurers, brokers, and other industry participants in risk assessment, underwriting, claims, and regulatory compliance.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Verisk’s strategic priorities include driving consistent and predictable growth within insurance, modernizing core solutions with cloud and AI technologies, expanding into adjacent markets (e.g., life insurance, specialty, resilience, and sustainability), and disciplined capital allocation. R&D efforts focus on enhancing data assets, developing advanced analytics, and integrating new technologies such as generative AI and digital workflow tools.
categories.revenue_model: The company primarily generates revenue through annual subscriptions and long-term agreements for its hosted solutions, which accounted for approximately 80% of 2023 revenues. Additional revenue streams include transactional and advisory/consulting services, as well as licensing of proprietary data, software, and analytics platforms.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Verisk faces competition from internal insurer technology teams, other statistical agents and advisory organizations, regional property inspection providers, InsurTech firms, consulting and IT service companies, and specialized analytics vendors. The company differentiates itself through deep insurance expertise, integrated solutions, proprietary data, and long-standing industry relationships, maintaining a leading position in U.S. P&C insurance analytics.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Verisk reported revenues of $2.68 billion, representing a 7.4% increase over 2022, with an EBITDA margin of 53.1%. The company has a history of strong cash flow generation, significant operating leverage, and consistent growth, supported by recurring subscription revenues and strategic acquisitions. Following recent divestitures, Verisk is focused on scaling its insurance analytics business globally.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Verisk’s value proposition centers on its unique, proprietary data assets, deep insurance domain expertise, and integrated analytics and technology solutions that are embedded in client workflows. The company emphasizes its ability to improve client risk assessment, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and fraud detection, delivering measurable value and fostering long-term customer relationships.
